## 12 September 2008

## Circular to All Licensed Corporations and Registered Institutions

## Guidance on disclosure of relevant material information by licensed or registered persons to their clients

This is to remind licensed and registered persons of the requirement of General Principle 5 of the Code of Conduct, under which they are required to make adequate disclosure of relevant material information in their dealings with their clients.  Such disclosure is essential to help investors make informed investment decisions and we have previously included this as one of the six suitability obligations expected of investment advisers 1 in our FAQs entitled 'Suitability Obligation of Investment Advisers' published on 8 May 2007.

Under the current legal and regulatory regime in Hong Kong, a financial product or an offering document of a financial product has to meet applicable requirements before it can be authorized by the Commission. The Commission therefore takes the view that the authorization status (that is, whether or not the product or offering document has been authorized by the Commission) should form part of the relevant material information to be disclosed by all licensed and registered persons in their dealings with their clients.

We have updated the Intermediaries Supervision Related FAQs (under Topic 10) as published on the website of the Securities and Futures Commission accordingly.

Should you have any queries regarding the contents of this circular, please contact Ms Lorraine Chan at 2842-7751.

Intermediaries Supervision Department Securities and Futures Commission

SFO/IS/018/2008

1 Defined as licensed and registered persons who are engaged in financial planning and wealth management business activities relating to the provision of investment advice, making of recommendations and/or solicitation
